It adds up to around 1600 meters of land border between Sweden and Finland around Haparanda.  It is an approximate lenght because I measured them all on Google Maps. Some parts are marshland or areas with reeds. What is land is not obvious from aerial photographs

replies.author: @Damsov-ph2ry
replies.text: @Richard-g3b5p I’ve done some further research, and buffer zones cannot be classified as state borders. According to the official definition, while they are not terrae nullius (even though they are mentioned in the Wikipedia article on that subject), they do not belong to anyone either. Under international law, buffer zones are specially designated, demilitarized areas established by treaty within existing state or mandated territory; as such, they belong to no one, yet they are not terrae nullius. And you are absolutely right: the border between Gaza and Egypt is also a buffer zone, and therefore it, too, should not have been included in this video. Consequently, the whole thing still doesn’t really make much sense.
